title: Gradient descent: two learning rates on the same bowl
description: A long, narrow bowl-shaped loss surface, drawn with contour lines. A blue ball and an orange ball start at the same point on the bowl's side, drawn side by side. Each step, each ball moves downhill against the gradient with its own learning rate and adds a point to its trail. A small rate creeps slowly toward the lowest point. A larger rate zigzags across the steep walls. A rate above 0.5 swings higher each step until the ball leaves the surface. Readouts show each ball's loss, the step count and each ball's status.
assumptions: Illustration: a simple made-up bowl, not a loss from a real trained model.

Loss = (x² + 4y²)/2, so the bowl is 4 times steeper along y (drawn left to right on screen) than along x. The lowest point is the centre, loss 0. The surface is drawn at 0.1 × loss over x, y from −4 to 4.
Each step: x ← x − rate·x, y ← y − rate·4y, with the exact gradient (no noise, no momentum). Both balls start at x = −3, y = 1.5, where the loss is 9. The run takes 5 steps a second.

A run ends after 60 steps. A ball stops early when its loss drops below 0.001 (converged) or when it leaves the drawn square |x|, |y| ≤ 4 (diverged). On this bowl any rate above 0.5 diverges and any rate below it converges.
A diverged ball is drawn held at the edge of the surface, but its Loss readout shows the true value. Changing either learning rate starts both runs again from the start, with the trails cleared.
When both balls are at the same point (at the start, or both at the bottom), they are drawn 0.2 to either side along x so both stay visible; the trails show the exact positions.
